title: The Little Beaver Builds a Home

pages.text: This is {name}. {name} is a round little brown beaver with two big front teeth and a flat, paddle-shaped tail. Willows whisper over the quiet forest river, and the day begins soft and warm. The water sparkles in the sunlight, and the air smells of willow leaves and cool river freshness. {name} breathes in the gentle air and smiles at the new day.

Today {name} has a big idea — to build a very first home. Here on the quiet river, among willows and reeds, is the perfect spot. The little heart beats faster at the very thought of a home of one's own. {name} imagines how cozy it will be to listen to the river from inside. "This is where my home will be," {name} dreams softly.

{name} dips into the cool water — splash, splash! — and carries the first little branch to the bank. Then another, and another. The water tickles the fur so nicely, and tiny bubbles race between those little paws. "Every branch is like a little treasure," thinks {name}. That flat paddle tail slaps the water happily.

Branch by branch, the little pile grows bit by bit. {name} stacks them carefully, one upon another. The air smells of wet wood and fresh river water. The sun warms that wet little back, and the work feels even merrier. {name} hums a soft little tune without words — work goes easier with a song.

On a green reed a tiny bird sways and chirps cheerfully. {name} smiles up at it with those big front teeth. "Chirp-chirp!" rings the little song right over the water. The work is going well, and the little heart feels light. It is lovely to work while someone sings nearby. The reeds sway in time, as if singing along.

But then the river sighs softly, and a little wave rolls onto the bank — splash! The branches wobble, drift apart, and float away. The pile comes undone right before those eyes. {name} blinks: a moment ago there was a pile — and now it is gone. The branches bob on the ripples like tiny boats. But the river is not unkind — it is simply big and playful.

{name} watches the branches drift across the water. That tail droops low, and there is a tickle in the throat. The water laps gently by those little paws, as if trying to comfort. But {name} takes a deep breath and says, "It's all right. I'll try again." Somewhere under the wet fur, a new bit of courage quietly wakes up. The river keeps humming its soft, friendly song, and everything already feels a little brighter. {name} looks over the calm water and holds that small warm feeling close.

And so {name} dives back into the water — splash, splash! Branch after branch comes back to the bank. Tap-tap — {name} stacks them tighter than before. The little paws already know their work, and the job goes faster. "Now I know a better way," {name} tells each little branch.

This time the pile comes out taller and neater. {name} presses the branches down with little paws and even packs the gaps with soft mud. The mud is warm from the sun and settles snugly between the branches. {name} steps back and looks the work over from every side. "Now it will surely hold," thinks {name}.

But the river stretches playfully once more — and a new wave licks the bank. The branches shift, the mud softens, and the pile slides gently into the water. This time {name} does not even manage to say a thing. Only tiny bubbles pop softly where the pile has just been. Time to start all over again.

{name} sits down on the wet sand and sighs. The sand is warm from the sun and gently warms those little paws. The little bird looks down from the reeds and chirps softly, as if to say, "Don't be sad." {name} thinks for a moment — and a new idea appears. It is still tiny, like a little seed, but it is already warm.

"Maybe this is too hard alone," thinks {name}. "What if I ask for help?" The idea feels warm and a little tickly, like a sunbeam. At that thought, even the little tail lifts more cheerfully. {name} stands up on those little paws with new resolve. The river laps nearby, as if to cheer: "Try it, try it!"

{name} walks along the bank and calls out brightly, "Hello, friends! Who will help me build a home?" The call floats over the water, among the willows and reeds. The echo runs across the water all the way to the far bank. For a moment it is very, very quiet — only the reeds whisper in reply. And then someone peeks out from behind the reeds.

First comes a sleek otter, gliding through the water. "I heard someone needs a hand!" she smiles. Her whiskers glisten with tiny droplets, and her eyes shine with curiosity. The otter can dive deep and carry the longest branches. "Building is what I love best!" she adds, and turns a merry circle in the water.

Next comes a kind old beaver, grey and wise. "A task is always lighter together," he says gently. His calm voice feels warm, like a soft blanket. "Together we will manage in no time," he adds with a solemn little nod. {name} claps that little paddle tail happily on the water.

"First we lay big stones, so the home stands strong," explains the old beaver, showing them how. {name} listens closely and rolls a round stone up onto the bank. The stone is heavy, but oh so sturdy. Thunk — the stone settles into place. "That's the way!" smiles the old beaver.

The otter brings long bendy branches, and the old beaver weaves them tight and strong. "Pass them here!" the otter calls cheerfully, and the branches settle one against another. {name} packs every little gap with soft mud. The warm mud squelches under little paws — squish-squish! Splash, tap, rustle — the work sings with many busy paws. Together the work goes faster — and it is far more fun.

Branch by branch, stone by stone — a round little home rises on the bank. It comes out neat and cozy, like a good little nut. The tiny bird circles above it and sings out brightly. {name} hops with joy. "How lovely our home is!" beams {name}.

And then the river rolls in with a wave once more — splash, splash! Everyone freezes for a moment. But the little home stands firm: not a single branch shifts. The wave laps against the stones and rolls gently back. "It stands! It stands!" whispers {name}, and the little heart skips with joy.

"Hooray! Our home is stronger than any wave!" laughs {name}. "Because we built it together!" smiles the old beaver warmly. The friends slap their tails happily on the water. The otter turns a happy somersault, and even the ripples seem to laugh along. Splash-splash-splash — the drops fly up like little silver sparks.

Little by little the sun sinks behind the willows, and the sky warms to gold. The water turns golden too, and the ripples lap more and more softly. The friends say goodbye until tomorrow. {name} stands by that little home and quietly thanks each one. "What a lovely day," thinks {name}. The tiredness today is a pleasant one — soft and warm.

Evening wraps the river in soft golden light. The reeds whisper quietly, and the water mirrors the first stars. {name} steps into that new little home — warm, dry, and cozy. Inside it is dim and soft, like a little nest. Behind the walls the river hums its quiet evening song.

{name} sits on that brand-new threshold and gazes at the quiet river. The little paws hum softly after all the work, and it is a pleasant hum. Inside it smells of fresh wood and warm mud. The little heart feels so warm, just like a hug. "This is my home," {name} whispers softly.

Far out on the water the friends can still be seen swimming home, and {name} waves a little paw. "See you tomorrow, friends!" {name} calls softly after them. Now {name} knows: the warmest homes are built with patience and friendship. And on the brand-new doorstep it feels warm, cozy, and not lonely at all. The eyelids grow heavy, like wet little branches, and the river whispers softer and softer.

The river gently rocks the stars on its water, and the little home stands sturdy and warm. {name} curls up snugly and gives a sweet little yawn. The little home creaks its branches ever so softly, as if humming a lullaby. The eyes close all by themselves, and the little paws grow warm and sleepy. Goodnight, little builder! Tomorrow — a new day on the quiet river.
